# Building and starting a tokamak
## Layout Place the core and put an [color=orange]HV cable[/color] under it so it joins the grid. The core, gyrotrons, injectors, harvesters and console all also need ordinary APC power. Anchor everything with a wrench.
Gyrotrons and injectors fire in a straight line in the direction they face. For one to work: - It must face the core along a row or column, in one of the four cardinal directions. - The core must be between one and seven tiles in front of it, and within about half a tile of the beam's centre line. - Rotate it with the rotate verb. It can be rotated while anchored.
The console lists every gyrotron and injector with an [bold]Aligned[/bold] or [bold]Not aligned[/bold] label, so check that before starting. A device that is not aligned does nothing.
Harvesters do not need to face anything but must be within 8 tiles of the core. The console finds the nearest core within 40 tiles of itself and controls every device within 40 tiles of that core.
## The console
The console shows the field state, plasma temperature, power output and draw, radiation, how full the field is, instability, and the contents of the plasma. Below that is a list of devices.
- [bold]Start field / Stop field[/bold] turns the magnetic field on or off. - [bold]Field strength[/bold] runs from 1 to 100. A stronger field raises power output and speeds up every reaction, but draws more APC power and adds instability. - [bold]SCRAM[/bold] dumps the field in an emergency. See [textlink="Hazards and shutdown" link="TokamakSafety"]. - Each gyrotron has an on/off toggle, a pulse rate (0.5 to 5 per second) and a pulse energy (1 to 10 MeV). - Each injector has an on/off toggle and an injection rate (0.5 to 10 units per second) and shows how full its rod is. - Each harvester has an on/off toggle.
You can also switch a gyrotron, injector or harvester on or off by using it directly. Examining one shows its settings. The console needs power like any computer.
## Heating Each gyrotron adds [bold]pulse rate × pulse energy × 400 kelvin[/bold] per second to the plasma. The plasma loses about 1% of its heat every second, so it settles at roughly 100 times the total heating per second. One gyrotron on its default settings (1 pulse per second at 1 MeV) only reaches about 40,000 K, which is not enough to ignite any fuel. Turn the settings up, or use more gyrotrons.
Gyrotrons draw APC power in proportion to what they fire, and injectors draw in proportion to their rate, so very high settings are not free.
Gyrotrons and injectors only act while the core's field is running.
## Start-up routine 1. Check the APC feeding the core and the devices is charged and has a backup. If the core loses power the field collapses. See [textlink="Hazards and shutdown" link="TokamakSafety"]. 2. Put a fuel rod in each injector. Deuterium-tritium rods are the easiest first fuel. 3. Open the console. Check every gyrotron and injector reads [bold]Aligned[/bold]. 4. Keep everyone away from the core, and wear radiation protection if anyone must stay close. 5. Set the field strength to a modest value, around 10 to 30, and press [bold]Start field[/bold]. The core hums and glows. 6. Turn the gyrotrons on, with enough pulse rate and energy to heat past the fuel's ignition temperature. 7. Turn the injectors on. Fuel enters the plasma at the injector's rate, up to the 400 unit limit. 8. Watch the temperature and instability. Once fusion starts, the reaction heats the plasma itself, so you can turn the gyrotrons down. 9. Power only appears on the grid while there is fuel in the plasma, and it rises as the plasma heats up.
An empty rod does nothing, so swap in a fresh rod before the plasma starves. A DT rod holds 100 units and lasts about 50 seconds at the default injection rate.
